It gives up Poland, the Baltic provinces, Finland, Ukraine — territory holding a large part of the Empire's population, coal and grain. It is signed because there is no army left with which to decline it. The front that could not be held in 1915 without shells could not be held in 1918 without men, and the men walked home.▶ SHOW THE MAPBaranovichiLvovGorliceMogilevBerdichevPskovTarnopolBrest-LitovskSettled recordEast Prussia: entered early, on the undertaking to France. 1915: the salient was given up and the army kept. August 1915: the Emperor assumed the supreme command in person. 1916: the South-Western Front attacked alone and stopped when exploitation stopped paying. March 1917: the front commanders advised abdication. June 1917: the offensive was made. Autumn 1914: Galicia was reinforced. The Emperor at headquarters: the capital did not hold together in his absence. The Second Army, August 1914: left to press on. The Carpathians, March 1915: halted in the passes to refit. The Guards, summer 1916: sent at the Stokhod for Kovel. Romania: three divisions sent. The death penalty: not restored. The Kornilov affair: the dismissal obeyed. Przemysl, winter 1914: assaulted. Lodz, November 1914: the Silesian offensive pressed on. East Prussia, Febr
